label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
**To the neighbours on Aughrim Terrace,**

Sorry to put this through every door, but as I don’t know who’s responsible, this is the fairest way to make the point without accusing the wrong person.

For about a month now, someone has been putting full black bags of their rubbish into my grey Greenmount bin at No. 14. It has **14 painted in white on the lid**, so there shouldn’t be any confusion about whose bin it is.

I put it out on Tuesday nights for collection on Wednesday morning. Last Tuesday, I got home from a gig at 3am to find three bags that weren’t mine crammed into it. The lid wouldn’t even close. One of the bags contained nappies.

This isn’t someone dropping in a wrapper or an empty coffee cup. It’s full bags, week after week.

Greenmount charges me by weight, at €0.41 a kilo. My latest bill was **€63.20 for two months**, when it’s normally around €25. I’m absolutely fuming that someone thinks it’s acceptable to leave me paying to get rid of their rubbish.

I work nights. Coming home late doesn’t mean I don’t notice what’s happening, and it certainly doesn’t mean I’m willing to put up with it.

To whoever is doing this: you know those bags aren’t mine, and you know you’re not the one getting the bill. Quietly making your rubbish somebody else’s expense is a rotten way to treat a neighbour.

If you’re stuck with your bin collection, ask. I’ll tell you who to ring. There are ways to sort it without sneaking bags into someone else’s bin.

**Stop putting your rubbish in my bin. Simple as that.** If it continues, I’ll be fitting a padlock. I’d rather not have to lock my own bin to stop a neighbour taking advantage, but I will.

To everyone who has nothing to do with this, apologies for the letter.

**No. 14**
